text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Syrian newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The higher Syrian-Iranian Comission discuss bilateral relations, the situation in the region and developments of the Arab-Israeli struggle. Syrian Vice-President Abdel-Halim Khaddam says what is happening in the West Bank is a result of the Oslo agreement.

- Syrian-Lebanese talks concluded by signing deals in transport and water sectors and an agreement to prevent double taxation. Syrian Prime Minister Mahmoud Zu'bi and Lebanese counterpart Rafik al-Hariri assure commitment to bolster cooperation.
- Arab media reports talk about an Israeli plan to hit strategic Arab targets.
- The export, import and consumption rationalisation committee passes new decisions to allow imports of raw sugar and ships.
- Experiments to plant coloured cotton in Syria.
- Condemnation to Israel's obstinate stands continues. Cairo says aggression against Syria would not be a picnic and Egyptian-Israeli ties are subject to collapse.
- Arab League warns Israel against escalating attacks on south Lebanon.
- Under false claims, Israel increases the budget of the "war ministry."
